protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Lalthanzuala Joshi
text: The recent air‑quality protests underscore the critical need for evidence‑based interventions. While stubble burning contributes significantly to particulate matter, vehicular emissions and industrial outputs remain major sources. A multi‑pronged approach—enhancing public transport, stricter enforcement of odd‑even rules, and incentivizing cleaner fuels—will be essential to reduce AQI levels below hazardous thresholds and safeguard public health.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air

text: Sure, add 1000 CNG buses—because that’ll magically clear the smog that even forced cricketers to wear masks!

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Abdul Sharma
text: I have seen the sky turn black during the stubble burning season, and the government even closed schools for a week in November 2021 because the AQI hit 362, showing how serious the problem is for workers like me.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Manoj Choudhary
text: Oh great, the BJP claims the AQI is fine while tankers spray water on monitors – as if that fixes the 491 reading on November 18, 2024!

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Sneha Ansari
text: Honestly, I think we all just need cleaner air for our families, no matter the politics – it's a basic right to breathe.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Abdul Haokip
text: The data is clear: on 18 November 2024 Delhi recorded a "severe plus" AQI of 491, the highest this year, and reports suggest BJP‑run tankers were seen spraying water near monitoring stations to lower the numbers. Such manipulation undermines public trust and shows why immediate, transparent action is essential for workers and farmers alike.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Gurpreet Thomas
text: According to the Supreme Court records, on 18 November 2021 the AQI reached 362, prompting the court to reprimand both central and state governments and ask for stricter measures. This factual backdrop highlights the ongoing gap between policy promises and on‑ground air quality, justifying continued protest and demand for accountability.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Fatima Haokip
text: The recent 491 AQI reading on 18 November 2024, labelled "severe plus," was the highest in Delhi for the year, and eyewitnesses reported BJP‑affiliated tankers spraying water at monitoring sites. This suggests deliberate data distortion, reinforcing why students and citizens must keep pressing for genuine transparency and effective pollution controls.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Suresh Choudhary
text: Last year my family in Punjab tried the new R‑device before the rice harvest; it cut down the smoke we used to see every morning. Yet when Delhi hit an AQI of 491 in November 2024, even that technology couldn't help us, and we felt the same choking breath as Delhiites, proving the need for nationwide solutions.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air
author: Manoj Reddy
text: Enough! Government lies while we suffocate!

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air

text: Just saw the AQI jump to 491 on 18 Nov 2024 – the worst of the season – and rumors say tankers were spraying water to hide it. Can't trust the numbers any more!

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air

Government ne 1000 extra CNG buses lane ka wada kiya hai, lekin hum abhi bhi saans ki takleef se jujh rahe hain. Humein turant action chahiye, warna humari health khatam ho jayegi.

School ki chhuttiyon ke baad bhi, humari family ko saans lene ke liye mask aur air purifier kharidna padta hai. Yeh sirf ek protest nahi, humari zindagi ki zaroorat hai ki sarkar is masle ko hal kare.

protest_title: Delhi Air Pollution Protest — Right to Breathe Clean Air

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Fatima Verma
text: The recent protests reflect deep concern over the Manipur violence, where as of 9 May the state reported over 60 deaths and at least twenty‑seven churches were destroyed, according to journalist Moses Lianzachin. The demand for central intervention aligns with documented grievances from both Meitei and Kuki communities, highlighting a need for impartial mediation and protection of displaced civilians. A comprehensive inquiry could clarify the roles of militias and security forces, fostering a sustainable peace process.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Nikita Patil
text: I remember when I first moved to Gujarat, my father told me stories of protests in the north that seemed distant. Seeing the Manipur demonstrations on TV reminded me of his words: 'Every citizen's voice matters, even if it's far from home.' It made me realize that solidarity isn’t bound by state lines; we all share the same hope for safety and justice for those affected.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Karthik Qureshi
text: The Manipur unrest, as documented, resulted in over 60 fatalities by 9 May and the destruction of at least twenty‑seven churches, indicating a severe escalation of ethnic tensions. The government's description of the situation as "relatively peaceful" on 10 May appears inconsistent with these figures. A thorough, independent investigation is essential to address both the immediate humanitarian crisis and the underlying political grievances, ensuring accountability and long‑term stability.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Abdul Das
text: Violence in Manipur hurts all of us, regardless of where we live. I hope the central government listens to the pleas for peace and justice, and that communities can rebuild trust through dialogue and genuine reconciliation.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Sourav Namgyal
text: The ongoing clashes in Manipur underline the need for a balanced approach: central intervention, respect for tribal rights, and accountability for any political rhetoric that fuels division. Only then can we hope for lasting peace.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Lalthanzuala Mishra

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

The violence has already taken the shape of a civil war, with both sides arming themselves, some with licensed guns and others with advanced weapons. It is essential that any solution respects human rights and addresses the root causes of mistrust between the communities.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Moumita Kumar
text: Oh great, another day, another headline about 77 Kukis and 10 Meiteis dying in the first week—just what we needed to boost tourism, right?

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Arjun Banerjee
text: The protests against the Manipur violence raise valid questions about state responsibility. While I sympathize with the victims, it is crucial to examine whether the central government's response has been proportionate and timely. The involvement of political figures with groups like Arambai Tenggol suggests a deeper politicisation of ethnic tensions, which must be addressed through transparent investigations and accountability mechanisms.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Pooja Patil
text: As an ex-serviceman from Manipur, I can confirm that the violence has escalated beyond isolated incidents. Reuters reported 77 Kukis and 10 Meiteis dead in the first week, and by 18 May Kuki legislators demanded a separate administration. Both communities are now armed, with some possessing licensed guns and others advanced weapons, turning the conflict into a de facto civil war that requires urgent federal intervention.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Mary Choudhary
text: I drive my auto-rickshaw through towns where I once sold tea to Kuki and Meitei families alike. After the May clashes, I saw homes burnt in Torbung and heard about five BSF companies arriving. The fear is real; even my own brother, a police officer, was injured. We need real protection, not just promises, for everyday people like us.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Harleen Joshi
text: I have watched the news about Manipur while cooking in my kitchen in Bihar, and the images of families losing everything hurt me deeply. As a homemaker, I feel we must stand with the victims and pray for peace, because any violence tears the fabric of our whole nation.

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Dolkar Kumar
text: Oh great, another protest while the shops are closed—just what the economy needed, right? (Accurate fact: The parliamentary opposition filed a no‑confidence motion on 10 August 2023 to press Modi to address the Manipur crisis.)

protest_title: Manipur Violence Protest — Demand for Peace and Justice
author: Kavya Iyer
text: The Manipur crisis illustrates how media narratives can inflame ethnic tensions. Local Meitei-owned outlets have labeled Kuki civilians as "aliens," and even the chief minister has echoed such dehumanising language, which scholars link to state‑enabled violence. This rhetoric undermines any prospects for reconciliation and highlights the need for impartial reporting and federal intervention.
